name: Power and control cable systems
principle: Cable systems move power and signals between equipment and boards. Construction is chosen per duty: XLPE or EPR insulation for power, fire-resistant (circuit integrity) cables for safety circuits that must keep working during a fire, armoured and lead-sheathed designs for direct burial and submarine routes, and segregated tray/ladder routing with derating for bunching, ambient temperature and harmonic heating. Standards such as IEC 60502 (1–30 kV) and IEC 60332 (fire behaviour) govern selection and testing.

process_steps.name: Cable type, size and rating selected for load, voltage drop and fault level
Routes engineered with segregation by voltage class and fire zoning
Cable installed, glands and terminations made
Insulation resistance and withstand tests prove the circuit

performance.basis: TNB MV distribution voltages for cable rating
TNB LV supply for LV power and control cables

limitations: cable is a fire load itself, so routing, coating and circuit-integrity classes are safety decisions
harmonic-rich drives and long runs derate neutrals and raise sheath losses
advantages: complete, testable, re-routable distribution without overhead lines
submarine and umbilical cable technology carries subsea power over tens of kilometres
